contact_edits.before: There's a third leading character who's said to be a critic by trade but spends his time hanging out with the stars and receiving their confidences; the job has certainly gone downhill in the last century or so. Diego Matamoros' role is similar to the one he had in The Play's the Thing, but this one's been removed from the controlling centre to the suffering sidelines. Anyway, in an evening where metatheatrics are already running riot, it's a pleasure to watch another instalment in the long-running, and constantly shifting, Schultz-Matamoros double act; no two actors play better together. A good supporting cast includes Dawn Greenhalgh as Ilona's dresser turned surrogate-mother (and Nandor's newly acquired and fearsome mother-in-law); Michael Simpson as an obsequious debt-collector who can be bought off with complimentary tickets; and Jennifer Phipps as an usherette who conveys, mostly in silence, that she knows exactly what she's worth and won't take a pfennig less. Camellia Koo's sets and Judith Bowden's costumes redeem the reputation of chocolate-box design: apt for a play with a sweet surface and a hard centre. - The Guardsman is in repertory at the Young Centre through Oct. 24. Visit youngcentre.caor call 416- 866-8666 for show times and ticket information.
